critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now well over 10,000 lines. The ask_copilot helper (lines 7564-7700) shares ~80% of its structure with the findings inventory builder (per-page <page n=X> markers, file_id tagging, source=box hint, char budget). Extract the inventory builder into a shared helper backend/services/vault_inventory.py — duplicated code paths between Findings and Co-pilot is exactly the kind of drift that caused the 30-file cap miss in the first place.

FILE_CAP=200 is now a magic constant scattered in ask_copilot. Surface it as DOCUMENT_INVENTORY_CAP in a constants module (or top-of-file constant) so future endpoints (research briefs, outreach generation, vault Q&A in the buyer console) consume the same value. The current Findings-vs-Copilot 200/200 parity is correct but easy to drift again on the next feature.

The dynamic char budget (150K total / N files) is a fixed per-call ceiling; large institutional vaults at 200 files still get only 750 chars per file which truncates structured tables (financials, term sheets) mid-row. Consider a two-tier budget: K-most-relevant files (BM25/embedding-ranked) get a wider slice, the rest a summary line — same total budget, much higher precision on the cited files. Not a blocker for this iteration.

Page-aware citation parser (server.py ~7660) silently falls back to page=1 when the model returns the legacy [filename] form. This is correct for backwards-compat with old messages in history, but the test suite should also assert the parser handles malformed cases like [p.3] (no filename) and [filename p.abc] (non-integer page) gracefully — neither is currently exercised in test_copilot_data_access.py.

Backfill clone (_clone_listing_files_into_room) now fires on every POST /copilot call regardless of room status. Confirmed by test (e). However it runs synchronously inside the request — if a vault adds 50+ new Composio-mirrored files between turns, the buyer's next copilot message will block on clone + Claude. Should be moved to a background task or an idempotent 'is_clone_in_sync' check that skips the clone when the listing and room have identical file inventories.

test_copilot_live.py reuses the same room across all three tests; if Mira (seller) purges 'Backfill Test Co' or the demo sweeper hits it mid-suite, all three tests will skip silently. Consider creating a per-suite test room as a fixture to remove that external dependency.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_copilot_live.py is the canonical live regression for the Co-pilot data-access fix. Run via `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_copilot_live.py -v -p no:warnings`. The test asserts (a) 200 response with assistant_message.citations[i] containing {file_id, filename, page}, (b) at least one citation overlaps with a real vault file_id, (c) latency < 100s (Cloudflare edge timeout) and < 60s for small vaults. rca of the issue: Original RCA (verified during this iteration): Co-pilot's ask_copilot helper hard-coded a 30-file inventory cap whereas Findings used 200; older Composio-mirrored files were silently dropped from the prompt, so Co-pilot answered 'no documents' or omitted them. Fix raised the cap to 200 to match Findings, added <page n=X> markers per file (same pattern Findings already uses), updated the COPILOT_SYS prompt to require [filename p.N] citations, added a page-aware citation parser with legacy fallback (page=1), and runs the backfill clone regardless of room status so newly-mirrored files always reach the Co-pilot context. Dynamic char budget (150K total / N files) keeps end-to-end latency at 4-13s for ≤30 files — well inside Cloudflare's 100s edge timeout.
